data.blockersTitle: Before you can delete your account:
data.confirmPrompt: Type your username, {{username}}, to confirm. Everything only you could see is deleted for good.
data.deleteDescription: Permanently deletes your account, your projects and tasks, and your settings. Tasks and comments you added to other people's projects stay there without your name. This can't be undone: download your data first if you want a copy.
data.exportDescription: A ZIP with all your projects, tasks (completed ones too), comments, labels, filters, settings and attached files, as JSON plus a spreadsheet-friendly CSV. Passwords and keys are never included.

apps.description: Apps and AI assistants you allowed to use your account. Removing one signs it out.

tokens.allProjects: All my projects, including new ones
tokens.copyNow: Copy your new token now. It won't be shown again.
tokens.description: For scripts and tools such as n8n or Home Assistant. Treat a token like a password.
tokens.fullAccessNote: Full access covers your whole account, so it can’t be limited to projects.
tokens.limitNote: It can’t see or change anything else: not your other projects, labels, filters or settings, and it can’t create projects. Sub-projects need ticking too.
tokens.title: Personal access tokens

webhooks.copySecret: Copy your signing secret now. It won't be shown again.
webhooks.description: BokyDo POSTs a signed JSON payload to your endpoint for each event you choose, in projects you can see. Verify the X-BokyDo-Signature header; see the webhook docs on your server for examples. Endpoints must be public https addresses.
webhooks.removeMessage: Events will no longer be sent to {{url}}.
webhooks.rotateMessage: The old secret stops working immediately. Your endpoint must be updated with the new one.
webhooks.testQueued: Test delivery queued — it will arrive within seconds.
webhooks.title: Webhooks

notifications.pushDenied: Notifications are blocked for this site in your browser settings. Allow them there, then come back.

notifications.reportEnabled: Email me a report written by AI

calendar.deleteMessage: The link stops working at once. Calendars subscribed to it will go empty.
calendar.feedsDescription: Subscribe to a project or saved filter from Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Thunderbird or any app that can subscribe to a calendar link. Tasks with a due date appear as events and the calendar refreshes by itself. Anyone with a link can see those tasks' titles and dates without signing in, so treat it like a password. You can reset or delete a link at any time.
calendar.includeHint: Off by default: descriptions are shared with the calendar app and its servers.
calendar.none: You have no calendar feeds yet.
calendar.noneYetHint: Create a saved filter first (Filters & Labels).
calendar.onlyShownOnce: This is the only time the link is shown. If you lose it, reset the link to get a new one.
calendar.resetMessage: You get a new link and the old one stops working at once, so any calendar subscribed to it must be updated.
calendar.targetGoneNote: The project or filter was deleted or is no longer shared with you, so this link shows nothing.

security.breachCheck: Reject passwords found in data breaches
security.breachCheckHint: Checks Have I Been Pwned. Only the first 5 characters of a hash of the password leave this server.
security.loginAlerts: Email users about sign-ins from new places
security.mfaHint: Users without an authenticator app or passkey are asked to set one up before they can continue.

push.allowedHostsHint: One per line: a hostname (ntfy.example.com), optionally with a port (:8443) or *. for its subdomains. HTTPS only. A listed server may be on your private network.
push.description: Browsers push through their vendor's service (Google, Mozilla, Apple, Microsoft), which always works. The Android app can also use UnifiedPush through a distributor such as ntfy; list the push servers it may use here. Notifications are end-to-end encrypted, but the server will send requests to these hosts, so only list push servers you trust.
push.title: Push services

users.createdIntro: Give them this one-time passphrase. They must choose their own password when they first sign in. It won’t be shown again.
users.deleteDescription: Deletes the account and everything only they could see. Their tasks and comments in shared projects stay without their name. They get an email if they have a verified address.
users.deleteBlockers: First, they (or the project owners) must transfer or delete: {{items}}{{extra}}.
users.emailHint: With email set up, the invitation is sent for you.
users.inviteEmailed: Sent to {{email}}. You can also share this link; it works once, for 7 days.
users.inviteLink: Share this link; it works once, for 7 days.
users.resetLinkIntro: Send this link to the user over a channel you trust. It works once, for 24 hours.
users.title: Users

backups.description: Backups hold everything (database, attachments and this server's keys), encrypted with your passphrase, in the server's data folder. Download copies and keep them somewhere else too: a backup on the same disk doesn't survive losing that disk.
backups.newPassphrase: New backup passphrase (leave empty to keep it)
backups.passphraseHint: At least 12 characters. Keep it safe and away from the server: without it no backup can be restored, and changing it doesn't re-encrypt older backups.
backups.passphraseWarning: Set a passphrase: automatic backups don't run without one.
backups.restoreDescription: Everything on this server is replaced by {{name}}{{created}}. Changes made since then are lost; a backup of the current state is made first. Everyone is signed out, and API tokens and connected apps have to be set up again.
backups.restoreSuccess: Restored. The server is restarting; you'll be taken to sign in.

restoreError.backup_passphrase_or_damaged: The passphrase is wrong, or the file is damaged.
restoreError.backup_incompatible: This backup comes from a newer or different BokyDo; restore it on a matching version.
restoreError.backup_invalid: That file isn't a usable BokyDo backup.

backups.title: Backups

import.notesArchived: Archived in Todoist, so skipped by default.
import.notesImportedAs: Imported before into {{name}}. Only tasks not brought over yet are added.

import.projectsHint: Found {{projects}}, {{tasks}}, {{sections}} and {{comments}}. Projects set to Skip are not imported.

import.noOthers: No one else is on this Todoist account’s projects.

import.runDefault: The import stopped unexpectedly. Start it again to finish.
import.templatesSubtitle: Start a project from a template or a CSV file
import.csvDescription: Choose a project exported from Todoist, or a file in the same format (up to 1,000 rows and 1 MB). You see what it holds before anything is added. Exporting works the other way: open a project's menu and choose “Export as CSV”.
import.readFailed: That file could not be read.
